source_text:
9.1 μιξηαελις πσελλι ιν Περὶ παραδόξων ἀναγνωσμάτων Σύλληψιν ἐργάζεται μὲν
Θεὸς καὶ Φύσις, ὡς ἔγωγε πέπεισμαι, Ἀφρικανὸς δέ φησιν ὅτι καὶ τεχνική τίς ἐστι
γέννησις, καὶ γεννηθήσεται τεχνικῶς εἰ ὁ ἀνὴρ μέλλων εἰς συνουσίαν ἐλθεῖν
ἐπιχρίσοι τὸ μόριον αἵματι λαγωοῦ ἢ χηνείῳ στέατι· ἀλλ' ἐκείνως μὲν ἄρρεν, οὕτω
δὲ θῆλυ. Κατάγει δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος καὶ γάλα ἐκ μαστῶν τεχνικῇ μεθόδῳ καὶ
σπαργῶντας μετὰ τὸν τοκετὸν σβεννύει κηρωτῇ κυπρίνῃ. Ποιεῖται δὲ καὶ ἄτοκον
γυναῖκα ἀτόκιον αὐτῇ περιάπτων· τοῦτο δέ ἐστι βατράχου ἐγκέφαλος ῥάκει
περιειλημμένος λινῷ. Καὶ ταῖς δυστοκούσαις γαγάτην λίθον τῇ ἀριστερᾷ ἐγχειρίζων
χειρὶ ὠκυτοκεῖν ταύτας ἐργάζεται. Πεποίηται δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ συλληπτικὰ ἕτερα
μίγματα καὶ τεχνάσματα καὶ παιδοται δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ συλληπτικὰ ἕτερα μίγματα καὶ
τεχνάσματα καὶ παιδοποιητικὰ ἔμπλαστρα. Ἔστι δὲ αὐτῷ ἴσχαιμόν τι ἐξ ἀκρεμόνων
συκαμίνου συντεθειμένον τῶν φωστήρων ὑπὸ γῆν ὄντων περίαπτον· διδοῖ δὲ αὐτῷ
τὴν δύναμιν ἐπωδῇ τινι ἀπορρήτῳ. Βάπτει δὲ καὶ τρίχας λευκὰς ἐκ λιθαργύρου
κεκομμένης. Ποιεῖται δὲ καὶ φωνασκικὸν ἐξ ἴρεως καὶ τραγακάνθης. Ἰοῖ δὲ καὶ τὸν
χρυσὸν σιέλῳ λυττῶντος κυνός. Ἀντιπαθές τε ποιεῖται θηρίων πληγαῖς τῇ
διπροσώπῳ ἐμπλάστρῳ. Καὶ σκορπιακά τινα ὀνομάζει παράδοξα. Καί τινα ἔλεγχον
ποιεῖται κλεπτῶν ἀφανῶν, γυρίνων βατράχων τὰς γλώσσας ἀποτέμνων καὶ
ταριχεύων, εἶτα ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ἀλφίτοις ἀναμιγνὺς καὶ τοῖς ἐν ὑπονοίᾳ τῆς ὑφαι
ρέσεως τοῦ ζητουμένου προδιδούς· Καὶ ὁ ἀφελόμενος, φησί, τὸ φώριον ἐν ἐκστάσει
ὥσπερ γενόμενος ἑαυτὸν ἀριδήλως δημοσιεύει· ὀνομάζει δὲ τὸ βρῶμα
«κλεπτέλεγχον». Καὶ περὶ γεωργίας δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος λέγει παράδοξα. Συκάμινα γάρ,
φησί, λευκὰ φέρει συκάμινος δεξαμένη λεύκην ἐγκεντρισθεῖσαν· τὰ αὐτὰ δὲ ἐνέγκοι
καὶ λεύκη ἐν ᾗ ὀφθαλμισθείη συκάμινος. Κατάγραπτα δὲ ἐρυθρότατα περσικὰ
γίνεται, εἰ καταγράψεταί τις τὸν ἐγκείμενον τῇ πυρίνῃ καρπόν. Καταπαύει δὲ καὶ
λοιμὸν ἢ ὀπῷ βαλσάμου ἢ συνοχῇ δυσώδει τῇ βυρσοδεψικῇ τοῖς ἐναντίοις. Σκευάζει
δὲ καὶ οἶνον παντοδαπόν, τὸν μὲν νάρδου στάχυι, τὸν δὲ σχίνου ἄνθει, καὶ ἄλλον
ἑτέρῳ φαρμάκῳ. Πλάττει δὲ καὶ ὑακινθίνας λίθους καὶ σμαραγδίνας καὶ
σαρδώνυχας. Θεραπεύει τε ἀσπίδων δήγματα καὶ ἀχλὺν ὀφθαλμῶν οὐ τοῖς
ἐγνωσμένοις φαρμάκοις ἀλλὰ περιάπτοις τισὶ καὶ ἐπᾴσμασιν.
pass_a_gloss: 9.1 Michaelis-Pselli in Concerning of-paradoxical readings. Conception works yes God and Nature, as I-at-least have-been-persuaded, Africanus but says that also a-technical some is generation, and it-will-be-generated technically if the man being-about into intercourse to-come should-smear the member with-blood of-a-hare or with-goose fat; but in-that-way yes male, thus but female. Draws-down but this man also milk from breasts by-a-technical method and those-swelling after the childbirth he-quenches with-a-cyprine cerate. He-makes but also a-barren woman an-atokion to-her hanging-on; this but is of-a-frog a-brain with-a-rag having-been-wrapped in-linen. And to-the-ones-in-hard-labor a-gagate stone in-the left putting-into hand to-give-birth-quickly these he-works. Have-been-made but by-him also conception-other mixtures and devices and [lock unrestored: παιδοται] but by-him also conception-other mixtures and devices and child-making plasters. Is but to-him a-styptic something from twigs of-mulberry having-been-composed of-the luminaries under earth being an-amulet; he-gives but to-it the power by-an-incantation some unspeakable. He-dyes but also hairs white from litharge having-been-pounded. He-makes but also a-voice-training-remedy from iris and tragacanth. He-rusts but also the gold with-saliva of-a-raging dog. An-antipathetic also he-makes for-beasts' strikes with-the two-faced plaster. And scorpion-remedies some he-names paradoxes. And a-certain test he-makes of-thieves hidden, of-tadpoles of-frogs the tongues cutting-off and pickling, then upon the need with-barley-meal mixing and to-those in suspicion of-the taking-away of-the-sought giving-forth; And the one-having-taken-away, he-says, the stolen-thing in a-trance as-if having-become himself clearly publishes; he-names but the food 'thief-detector'. And concerning farming but this man says paradoxes. Mulberries for, he-says, white bears a-mulberry-tree having-received a-white-poplar having-been-grafted-in; the same-things but would-bear also a-white-poplar in which should-be-budded a-mulberry. Inscribed but most-red peaches become, if should-inscribe someone the lying-in the stone fruit. He-stops but also a-plague either with-sap of-balsam or with-confinement foul-smelling the tanner's by-opposites. He-prepares but also wine of-every-kind, the-one yes with-nard's spike, the but with-mastic's flower, and another with-another drug. He-fashions but also hyacinth-stones and emerald-ones and sardonyxes. He-treats also of-asps bites and mist of-eyes not with-the known drugs but with-amulets some and with-incantations.
pass_b_english: From Michael Psellus, On paradoxical readings. Conception is worked by God and Nature, as I at least am persuaded; but Africanus says that there is also a technical generation, and it will be generated technically if the man about to come to intercourse should smear the member with hare’s blood or with goose fat: in that way male, in this way female.

And this man also draws down milk from breasts by a technical method, and those swelling after childbirth he quenches with a cyprine cerate. He also makes a woman barren by hanging an atokion on her: this is a frog’s brain wrapped in a linen rag. And to those in hard labor, putting a gagate stone into the left hand, he makes them give birth quickly. There have been made by him also other conception-mixtures and devices and [lock unrestored: παιδοται] and by him other conception-mixtures and devices and child-making plasters.

And he has a styptic thing composed from mulberry twigs, an amulet when the luminaries are under the earth; and he gives it its power by a certain unspeakable incantation. He also dyes white hairs from pounded litharge. He also makes a voice-training remedy from iris and tragacanth. He also rusts gold with the saliva of a rabid dog. And he makes an antipathetic for beasts’ strikes with the two-faced plaster. And he names certain scorpion-remedies as paradoxes.

And he makes a certain test of hidden thieves, cutting off the tongues of frog-tadpoles and pickling them, then at the time of need mixing them with barley-meal and giving them to those under suspicion of the taking-away of the thing sought. And the one who took away the stolen thing, he says, as if becoming in a trance, openly publishes himself; and he names the food “thief-detector.”

And about farming too this man says paradoxes. For a mulberry-tree, he says, bears white mulberries when it has received a grafted-in white poplar; and a white poplar in which a mulberry has been budded would also bear the same. And peaches become most-red inscribed, if someone inscribes the fruit that lies in the stone. He also stops a plague either with balsam sap or with the foul-smelling confinement of the tanner’s trade, by opposites. He also prepares wine of every kind, one with nard-spike, one with mastic-flower, and another with another drug. He also fashions hyacinth-stones and emerald-stones and sardonyxes. And he treats asp-bites and mist of the eyes not with the known drugs but with certain amulets and incantations.

choices.term: μιξηαελις πσελλι ιν Περὶ παραδόξων ἀναγνωσμάτων
choices.english: From Michael Psellus, On paradoxical readings
choices.why: Lock header is Latin Michaelis Pselli in written in Greek letters. This slice is Psellus reporting Africanus, not Africanus in his own voice, and not 'African knowledge'.

choices.term: σπαργῶντας μετὰ τὸν τοκετὸν σβεννύει κηρωτῇ κυπρίνῃ
choices.english: those swelling after childbirth he quenches with a cyprine cerate
choices.why: σπαργάω is swell (breasts), not σπαργανόω swaddle. He stops the swelling with henna/cyprus cerate; he does not extinguish newborns.
rejected: swaddling and extinguishing newborns with Cyprian wax

choices.why: γαγάτης is jet. NV crib read durian.

choices.english: a mulberry-tree … a grafted-in white poplar
choices.why: συκάμινος is mulberry, λεύκη white poplar, ὀφθαλμίζω bud-graft. Not figs or leeks.
rejected: white figs from figs receiving white grafts
leeks in which leeks are eyed

choices.term: Ἰοῖ δὲ καὶ τὸν χρυσὸν σιέλῳ λυττῶντος κυνός
choices.english: He also rusts gold with the saliva of a rabid dog
choices.why: ἰόω is rust/corrode, not gild. The paradox is that gold is stained by rabid-dog saliva.
σχῖνος is mastic/lentisk, not σκίλλα squill.

choices.term: ἀσπίδων δήγματα καὶ ἀχλὺν ὀφθαλμῶν … ἐπᾴσμασιν
choices.english: asp-bites and mist of the eyes … incantations
choices.why: ἀσπίς here is the asp. ἐπᾴσματα are charm-songs, not salves. NV crib had scorpion stings and salves.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
